references.text: God promises to punish the evil shepherds who do not care for the flock, which reflects Jesus' description of the hired hand's indifference.
The Lord accuses Israel's leaders of not caring for the sheep, a directly parallel theme to the hired hand's lack of concern for the flock.
The entire chapter is a judgment against bad shepherds who let the flock suffer, in contrast to the good shepherd who gives his life.
The Lord is the shepherd who cares for his sheep, standing in sharp contrast to the hired hand's indifference in John 10:13.
